findings.problem: ShardWorkflow has no typestate enum or discriminant; lifecycle is represented by independent booleans so any combination is possible including invalid states like is_validated=false with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Caller constructs ShardWorkflow { is_validated: false, is_sent: true } which represents an impossible workflow state, bypassing all invariants at compile time.
findings.fix: Replace status/is_validated/is_sent with a single ShardState enum with ordered variants (e.g., Created, Validated, Sent) and make ShardWorkflow hold ShardState. Remove the three fields entirely.

findings.problem: status is a pub String field. Any caller can set it to arbitrary values ("deleted", "", "SENT", null bytes) that have no meaning in the domain.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime logic branching on status string values can hit unexpected branches, causing incorrect behavior or silent corruption. Comparison is case-sensitive and whitespace-dependent.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub state: ShardState` where ShardState is a sealed enum with exactly the valid lifecycle variants. Remove all string equality checks.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be set in any combination (validated+sent, neither, only one), encoding invalid state machines.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent sets is_sent=true but does not check is_validated, so an unvalidated shard can transition to sent. Callers can set is_validated=true without ever calling validation logic.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a typestate enum ShardState { Created, Validated, Sent }. mark_sent should take ShardState::Validated as input and return ShardState::Sent, enforced at the type level.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is independent of the lifecycle booleans. A shard can have sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true — no coherence invariant.
findings.failure_mode: The timestamp field can drift from the actual lifecycle state. Deserializing JSON with only sent_at_epoch_ms creates a shard with a sent timestamp but is_sent=false, violating workflow invariants.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum: enum ShardState { Created, Validated, Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 } }. This makes the timestamp ownership co-located with the state that requires it.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive string with no domain semantics. Any string is valid including empty, duplicate, or malformed IDs. No newtype enforces ID constraints.
findings.failure_mode: Caller passes empty string "" or duplicate IDs, causing incorrect shard lookup or silent data corruption. String comparison for identity is fragile vs structurally distinct ID types.
findings.fix: Define `pub struct ShardId(String)` with a smart constructor `ShardId::from_str(s: &str) -> Result<ShardId, ParseError>` that validates non-empty format. Use `ShardId` in ShardWorkflow instead of `String`.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary into the domain. ShardWorkflow is constructible directly from untrusted input with zero validation, so callers can build invalid domain states.
findings.failure_mode: External data deserialized to ShardWorkflow can carry arbitrary status strings, invalid boolean combinations, and orphaned timestamps — no smart constructor enforces domain invariants at the boundary.
findings.fix: Replace the struct with a smart constructor `ShardWorkflow::new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>` that returns a fully validated domain value. The typestate enum ensures all fields are coherent by construction.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates item.status and item.is_sent directly without checking preconditions (e.g., is_validated must be true). It does not set sent_at_epoch_ms.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated shard gets marked sent with no error, no timestamp recorded, and status set to a raw string literal "sent" that could mismatch downstream string comparisons.
findings.fix: Signature should be `fn mark_sent(state: ShardState) -> Result<ShardState, WorkflowError>` returning Sent variant with timestamp. Caller provides current state; enum match enforces allowed transitions only.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists — trivial struct with no algorithmic complexity
no profiler data — no hot path to profile

no command-truth evidence — no benchmark or command output files present
no second-ring evidence — no integration tests or CLI harness
residual_risk: The entire domain model is representable in invalid states at compile time. The typestate pattern would eliminate all invalid state combinations by making them unrepresentable. Without the enum/typestate refactoring, any downstream code assuming valid shard lifecycle is fragile and error-prone. Static review only; no commands run.
